title: Amazon to Launch New Grocery-Store Business
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly planning to open dozens of new grocery stores in major U.S. cities, expanding its presence in the food business beyond Whole Foods. The first store is anticipated to open in Los Angeles by the end of the year, with at least two more planned for early next year. This new chain will be distinct from the company's existing Whole Foods unit, indicating a diversified approach to the grocery market.

title: Verizon Acquires ProtectWise for Network Detection and Response Services -
summary: Verizon Communications has acquired ProtectWise, a provider of cloud-based Network Detection and Response (NDR) cybersecurity services. ProtectWise, founded in 2013, had raised roughly $67 million and was known for its partner-centric strategy. This acquisition enhances Verizon's ability to detect and respond to security threats, particularly as it expands its 5G footprint.

title: Mist Systems joins Juniper Networks
summary: Mist Systems has been acquired by Juniper Networks for over $400M, marking a significant milestone for the company and its founders, Sujai Hajela, Bob Friday, and Brett Galloway. Lightspeed Venture Partners, an early investor, highlights Mist Systems' revolutionary AI-driven wireless networking technology, which powers major enterprises. This acquisition is seen as a validation of Mist Systems' vision to disrupt the networking industry with its "AI for IT" solutions.

title: Tech Moves: Leafly hires Amazon Prime Video vet as CEO; Former F5 CEO joins ExtraHop Board
summary: Leafly, a marijuana review and discovery platform, has appointed Tim Leslie, former VP of Amazon Prime Video International, as its new CEO. Additionally, John McAdam, former CEO of F5 Networks, has joined the board of directors of hybrid cloud security startup ExtraHop. These moves highlight significant leadership changes in the Pacific Northwest tech community.

title: Forbes' billionaires list includes 20 from Michigan
summary: Forbes' annual list of the world's richest people includes 20 individuals with ties to Michigan, ten of whom currently reside in the state. The article highlights each Michigan-connected billionaire, detailing their net worth, global ranking, and their connection to the Great Lakes State. Notable figures include Larry Page, Steve Ballmer, and various business leaders from prominent Michigan companies like Meijer, Quicken Loans, and Stryker Corp.

title: HEINZ Debuts Two A-MAYO-ZING Condiments to Satisfy Saucy Fans
summary: HEINZ is launching two new condiment mashups, MAYOCUE (mayonnaise and barbecue sauce) and MAYOMUST (mayonnaise and mustard), following the success of MAYOCHUP. These new sauces aim to provide convenient and pre-mixed flavor combinations for consumers. The 16.5oz bottles will retail for $3.49 and will be available at major retailers and online.

title: Donald A. Brown, co-founder of The JBG Cos., dies
summary: Donald A. Brown, co-founder of The JBG Companies, has died at the age of 90. He was instrumental in launching the precursor to JBG Smith Properties, a company now known as Amazon.com Inc.'s landlord and development partner. The article reflects on his legacy and the transformation of JBG into a major real estate player.

title: Family Dollar was once considered “Amazon-proof.” Now it’s closing hundreds of stores.
summary: Dollar Tree, the parent company of budget stores Dollar Tree and Family Dollar, announced the closure of 390 Family Dollar stores in 2019 following attempts to revamp the brand, signaling the difficulty of turning around struggling retail in today's landscape. The closures highlight the challenges brick-and-mortar stores face against online competitors like Amazon and aggressive pricing from Walmart, even for discount retailers once thought to be "Amazon-proof." Despite a $2.3 billion loss linked to the closures, Dollar Tree plans renovations and new product introductions to stay competitive, as rivals like Amazon and Walmart expand into budget-friendly categories.

title: Costco builds 'fulfillment automation center' to expand e-commerce
summary: Costco has opened a "fulfillment automation center" to enhance its e-commerce capabilities, signaling increased investment in its online business. This move comes despite previous statements from its CFO expressing a preference for in-store shopping. The new center aims to support the company's expanding digital presence.

title: Salesforce at 20 offers lessons for startup success
summary: Salesforce celebrated its 20th anniversary, marking its evolution from a nascent startup challenging CRM giants to a SaaS powerhouse with an annual run rate exceeding $14 billion. The article delves into its origins in a San Francisco apartment, its growth through pioneering cloud software, and the visionary leadership of Marc Benioff and his team. Key lessons for startups include the importance of long-term vision, building trust, strong company culture, and strategic growth through acquisitions.

title: Costco Raises Minimum Wage to $15 an Hour
summary: Costco Wholesale is increasing its minimum wage for store workers to $15 an hour, marking the second such increase in less than a year. This announcement followed the company reporting higher than anticipated second-quarter financial earnings with significant increases in net sales and income. The move is part of a trend among retail giants like Target and Amazon to offer better wages and benefits to attract skilled workers.

title: C.H. Robinson CEO John Wiehoff Takes Work And Play Seriously
summary: John Wiehoff, CEO of C.H. Robinson, believes a "work hard, play hard" mentality is crucial for both personal success and building a strong company culture. During his 17-year tenure as CEO, C.H. Robinson's stock price increased nearly sixfold and revenue grew significantly, a testament to his leadership and focus on long-term vision and a sustainable culture. Wiehoff, who is retiring from his CEO role, emphasizes integrity, leadership, and a commitment to employees, customers, and a broad network of mentors.

title: Nvidia acquires Mellanox against growing AI, data competition
summary: Nvidia has acquired Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing and competitive market for AI and data-intensive computing platforms. This merger aims to bolster their combined capabilities against new rivals like Amazon and Cray, as both companies already have a significant presence in high-performance computing (HPC) with their integrated technologies. The acquisition is seen as a strategic move to address increasing competitive challenges in the HPC market.

title: F5 Networks paying $670M to acquire NGINX, a web server that runs a big chunk of the internet
summary: F5 Networks is acquiring NGINX, a popular web server, for $670 million. This acquisition aims to transition F5 from a hardware company to one focused on software and services for application infrastructure, bridging app development and security across various cloud environments. NGINX will retain its brand and open-source strategy, with its leadership joining F5.

title: F5 Networks Acquires NGINX For $670 Million
summary: F5 Networks has acquired NGINX, a popular open-source web server company, for approximately $670 million. This acquisition aims to strengthen F5's growth trajectory by accelerating its software and multi-cloud transformation, bridging NetOps and DevOps with consistent application services. NGINX will maintain its brand and leadership, leveraging F5's global sales and channel infrastructure.

title: Goodbye Growing Pains: Hanes’ New Babywear Delivers Comfort and Innovation for Baby, Convenience and Savings for Parents
summary: Hanes, America's No. 1 apparel brand, has launched its new Ultimate Baby line, including Flexy and Zippin collections, delivering comfort and innovation for babies and convenience and savings for parents. These collections feature adjustable cuffs, flexible fabrics, expandable necks, and protective zip covers, designed to grow with babies for their first 24 months, simplifying sizing to four categories. Available exclusively on Amazon, the line aims to address common parental challenges like outgrown clothing and difficult outfit changes, leveraging HanesBrands' "Innovate to Elevate" process.

title: Omada Health adds connected blood pressure and blood sugar monitors to platform
summary: Omada Health has introduced FDA-cleared and cellular-connected blood pressure cuffs and glucometers to its platform, allowing users to upload real-time vital readings for better health advice from coaches. These new devices, which also include free test strips for glucometers, are part of programs launched last year to support the treatment of patients with hypertension and Type 2 diabetes. This move aims to streamline the user experience, building on Omada’s existing connected scale for diabetes prevention and competing with companies like Livongo.

title: From Bentonville to Seoul, Jay Jorgensen Becomes General Counsel of South Korea's Coupang
summary: Jay Jorgensen, former executive vice president and global chief ethics and compliance officer of Walmart Inc., has been appointed as the new general counsel for Coupang, South Korea's largest and fastest-growing e-commerce company. This move brings Jorgensen's extensive experience in retail and compliance, including building a world-class program at Walmart, to the rapidly expanding South Korean e-commerce giant. Coupang, often referred to as the "Amazon of South Korea," is reportedly eyeing an initial public stock offering in 2019 or 2020.

title: Top gamer 'Ninja' made $1 million to promote EA's 'Apex Legends' launch - source
summary: Top gamer Tyler Blevins, known as "Ninja," was reportedly paid $1 million by Electronic Arts Inc. to promote the launch of their new game "Apex Legends." This significant payment highlights the intense competition in the battle royale genre and the growing influence of professional gamers in promotional strategies, with EA's stock price and market value rising significantly after the game's launch. The game amassed 10 million sign-ups in three days and 50 million users within a month, demonstrating the success of this influencer-based marketing approach.

title: Your U.S. Equity Fund Is More Global Than You Think
summary: This article examines how U.S. equity funds are more globally exposed than commonly perceived by analyzing revenue streams by region. Morningstar's new proprietary data reveals that many popular U.S. index-tracking ETFs have significant revenue exposure outside the United States, particularly in emerging Asian markets and the eurozone. The analysis highlights that relying on a company's headquarters or stock listing alone provides a flawed picture of a fund's true geographic allocation.

title: If you’re tracking the S&P 500 instead of this fund, you’re leaving money on the table
summary: This article suggests that investors tracking the S&P 500 might be missing out on better returns by overlooking the Invesco QQQ Trust. It highlights the Invesco QQQ Trust as a successful and diversified fund. The piece also addresses concerns about tech stock valuations, noting they are lower than before the dot-com bubble burst.

title: Former Toys R Us Headquarters In Wayne Sold
summary: The former 191-acre Toys R Us headquarters in Wayne, New Jersey, has been sold, with the new, unnamed buyer planning to enhance the site for multiple uses. The campus previously housed the toy company's headquarters for 16 years. This sale follows Toys R Us's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in March 2018, which led to the closure of all its U.S. stores.

title: Argentinian Company Wants to Build the Amazon of Latin America
summary: MercadoLibre Inc., an Argentinian e-commerce company, is striving to become the "Amazon of Latin America." To achieve this, it is investing $2 billion in logistics and payments infrastructure to serve a market where many customers lack traditional banking access. The company aims to strengthen its regional foothold and defend against competition from e-commerce giants Amazon and Alibaba.

title: Netflix is valued like a tech company, but its CEO just said it was a media company
summary: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings stated that the company is a media company rather than a tech company, primarily due to its significant spending on content. This stance deviates from other major tech firms that prefer to label themselves as "platforms." Hastings' comments came in response to questions about regulating tech companies, potentially allowing Netflix to avoid some scrutiny faced by its peers.

title: Why Now Might Be a Good Time to Buy QQQ
summary: This article discusses reasons why the Invesco QQQ ETF could be a good investment. It highlights QQQ's focus on large-cap growth, particularly in technology and related sectors, its strong historical performance relative to the S&P 500, and its high liquidity. The article also touches on potential risks like sector concentration and higher volatility compared to broader market indices.

title: iShares U.S. Equity Factor Rotation Active ETF
summary: This article provides a comprehensive profile of the iShares U.S. Equity Factor Rotation Active ETF (DYNF), detailing its price, category, inception date, expense ratio, and AUM. It also includes sections on its top holdings, concentration analysis, valuation, dividend information, performance metrics, and ESG scores. The report offers an in-depth look at this active ETF's characteristics and comparisons to its peers.

title: How Netflix plans on owning your kids’ screen time
summary: Netflix is heavily investing in children's animation, spending an estimated $1.1 billion this year, to appeal to its broad global subscriber base and fend off competition. Unlike traditional studios, Netflix aims for a diverse range of content without a singular "brand" to cater to every household member's viewing preferences. The company is encouraging creators to pursue unique visions and is experimenting with new interactive features to engage young viewers.

summary: This article provides comprehensive real-time and historical data for the Xtrackers Artificial Intelligence and Big Data UCITS ETF (SIX: XAIX).
